steps.label: Provider
steps.short: How does the backend execute it?

samples.title: Find Alice's latest transactions
samples.description: A JSON caller asks for five transactions belonging to an account owned by Alice. The same request crosses the semantic pipeline before SQL is produced.

caller.title: The caller expresses a business question
caller.body: The caller does not write SQL or select physical tables. It supplies a structured request describing the outcome it needs.

intent.title: Intent makes the request explicit
intent.body: The JSON adapter turns the external payload into a read intent. Relationships, fields, predicates, ordering and pagination are explicit data rather than generated SQL.

semantic-model.title: The semantic model gives names and meaning
semantic-model.body: The intent is compiled against the application-facing model. This is where names such as Transaction, Account and Customer become known capabilities instead of arbitrary database identifiers.

authorization.title: Authorization constrains the operation
authorization.body: Authorization is evaluated before provider execution. The policy can preserve or reject fields and can contribute predicates that must remain true when the plan reaches the provider.

execution-plan.title: The provider-independent plan captures execution intent
execution-plan.body: Foundgine lowers the authorized request into an execution representation. It contains the relationship traversal, filter, order and pagination without becoming PostgreSQL- or SQLite-specific.

provider.title: The provider translates the plan into executable operations
provider.body: The SQL provider is now responsible for physical execution. Values remain parameters; the semantic pipeline has already decided what the operation means and what is allowed.

output.statement: SELECT ... FROM "Transaction" t0 INNER JOIN "Account" t1 ... WHERE ... = @p0 ORDER BY ... DESC LIMIT @__fg_limit

result.title: The result returns business data, not provider internals
result.body: The provider returns rows through the execution boundary. The example test verifies five descending transactions for Alice.

samples.title: Let an agent ask for customer data without SQL access
samples.description: An AI agent can produce intent, but the application remains the authority. This flow makes the security boundary visible: the model asks, Foundgine decides what the application will execute.

caller.title: The agent receives a natural-language task
caller.body: The model starts with a user request. It has no database credentials and no authority to invent a SQL query.

input.message: Find customer Alice and show her name and account balance

intent.title: The tool call becomes structured intent
intent.body: The agent selects an application capability. The structured payload is deliberately smaller than a database query and contains only semantic operations the capability exposes.

semantic-model.title: The application maps intent to its semantic surface
semantic-model.body: The agent cannot choose arbitrary persistence fields. The semantic model exposes Customer.name and Accounts.balance while internal fields can remain outside the contract.

authorization.title: Authorization decides what the agent may actually access
authorization.body: This is the trust boundary. The model's output is treated as untrusted input. Application policy determines visibility and tenant constraints before any provider call is made.

execution-plan.title: The authorized request becomes a provider-neutral plan
execution-plan.body: The plan carries the allowed projection and the tenant restriction forward. The agent never receives a way to bypass this layer by changing SQL text.

provider.title: The provider executes only the authorized plan
provider.body: SQL is produced after the semantic and authorization boundaries. The provider receives parameters and a constrained plan rather than an instruction from the model.

output.statement: SELECT customer.name, account.balance FROM customer JOIN account ... WHERE customer.name = @p0 AND customer.tenant_id = @tenant

result.title: The agent receives only the requested business result
result.body: The response can be returned to the application or agent without exposing database credentials, hidden fields or provider-specific control.
